statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 5% (low), Stress 38% (moderate), Confidence 85% (high). Every hour of the published horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path exists to score.
recommendation: Tail is published at a closed-venue floor and the mapped policy state remains EA_ON across all 24 published hours. No danger window is published, because no venue quotes at any point in the horizon and there is therefore no evidence-based interval to flag. The material forward checkpoints all sit beyond the final published hour: the Sunday 22:00 UTC CME restart, fifteen hours after the horizon ends, where Friday's hawkish payroll repricing and any accumulated Strait of Hormuz developments would be expressed as a single opening gap rather than as an observable path; the US Labor Day holiday on Monday 7 September, which delays the first full US cash session to Tuesday 8 September; and the resumption of the macro calendar with PPI and jobless claims on 10 September and CPI on 11 September ahead of the 15-16 September FOMC meeting. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 idle at 29,544.15 with CME futures settled since Friday 21:00 UTC; the full 24-hour horizon closes before the Sunday restart, so Tail holds a closed-venue floor while unpriced rate and energy risk lifts Stress
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having opened at 29,539.57, extended to 29,655.22, fully retraced that advance to a 29,440.15 low and recovered into the cash close. Retracement occurred repeatedly in both directions, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The August employment report, verified directly against the Bureau of Labor Statistics release, showed nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 55,000, the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1%, average hourly earnings up $0.10 on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% on the year, and upward revisions of 11,000 to June and 44,000 to July. Short-dated yields rose and reporting placed the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting near 58-60%, up from roughly 50% earlier in the week. The broad tape softened, with the Dow down 0.51% to 53,414.25 and the S&P 500 down 0.38% to 7,718.60, so the Nasdaq-100's small gain reflects narrow semiconductor-led strength offsetting sharp megacap losses rather than a broad advance. That internal split is a conflicting-breadth condition, which under this framework raises uncertainty rather than the probability of a one-way path. Carried volatility pricing is benign: the VIX closed at 14.53, up 1.47%, inside a 13.80-14.58 range. Federal Reserve H.15 constant maturities as of 3 September show the 2-year at 4.34%, the 10-year at 4.77% and the 30-year at 5.25%, with the 10-year adding about a basis point on Friday. The largest unpriced input is energy: WTI settled near $91.48 and Brent near $96.28, with WTI up roughly 9% on the week and about 21.6% on the month, alongside an unresolved Strait of Hormuz dispute in which Iranian officials have conditioned any reopening on sanctions relief, war reparations and an end to the regional conflict. No verified change to that position was observed by this assessment cutoff. CME equity index futures settled on Friday at 21:00 UTC and do not restart until Sunday 22:00 UTC, fifteen hours after the final published hour, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form at any point in this horizon. Tail is therefore held at a closed-venue floor of 4-5% and the mapped policy state is EA_ON throughout, while Stress drifts from 38% to 47% inside the moderate band to reflect hawkish September rate-path pricing and an unresolved energy premium carried unpriced across the weekend. Any restart repricing would arrive as a single opening gap, which is a discontinuity rather than the persistent mean-reversion failure the Tail score is defined to measure. Confidence is published at 85% and decays to 76% across the horizon: the evidence set is complete for a closed venue, with levels, yields, energy prices, the payroll release and the seven-day calendar each confirmed against primary sources this cycle, and the decay reflects only the ageing of Friday's marks. The shared cross-asset context file was older than its freshness window at run time, so this assessment rests entirely on independently verified primary sources.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span the second half of the August payroll session and the first eleven hours of the weekend halt. Tail ran 16-17% with Stress climbing from 58 to 62 through the pre-release European hours, peaked at Tail 24% and Stress 76% in the 12:00 UTC release hour under an event/whipsaw mode as the 162,000 payroll print landed against a consensus near 55,000, then decayed steadily through the US cash session as the index fully retraced its highs and recovered. By 20:00 UTC Tail was back to 12% with Stress at 48%, and from the 21:00 UTC CME settle the assessment moved to a closed-venue floor of Tail 5% and Stress 38%, held unchanged through the overnight hours. No hour required a mapped state beyond WATCH.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 38% to 47%, remaining inside the moderate band, reflecting hawkish September rate-path pricing and an unresolved Strait of Hormuz energy premium carried unpriced across the weekend. Confidence decays from 85% to 76% as Friday's verified evidence ages. The Sunday 22:00 UTC restart, the Monday US Labor Day holiday and the 8 September cash session all fall beyond the final published hour and will be scored by later cycles.
